spots.name: Sheffield Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of St Peter and St Paul, Sheffield, also known as Sheffield Cathedral, is the cathedral church for the Church of England diocese of Sheffield, England. Originally a parish church, it was elevated to cathedral status when the diocese was created in 1914.

names.ja: シェフィールド大聖堂

spots.name: Crucible Theatre
spots.summary: The Crucible Theatre, or simply The Crucible, is a theatre in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, which opened in 1971. Its name refers to crucible steel, which was developed in Sheffield in 1740 and drove the industrialisation of the city.

spots.name: Sheffield station
spots.summary: Sheffield station is a combined railway station and tram stop in the city of Sheffield, in South Yorkshire, England; it is the busiest station in the county and the third busiest in Yorkshire & the Humber, after Leeds and York. The South Yorkshire Supertram stop lies adjacent to the main station.

spots.name: Cathedral Church of St Marie

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of St Marie is the Roman Catholic cathedral in Sheffield, England. It lies in a slightly hidden location, just off Fargate shopping street, but signals its presence with a 195 feet (59 m) spire, the tallest in Sheffield.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral Church of St Marie, Sheffield

spots.name: Park Hill
spots.summary: Park Hill is a housing estate in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It was built between 1957 and 1961, and in 1998 was given Grade II* listed building status.

spots.name: Sheffield Town Hall
spots.summary: Sheffield Town Hall is a municipal building on Pinstone Street in the City of Sheffield, England. The building is used by Sheffield City Council, and also contains a publicly displayed collection of silverware. It is a Grade I listed building.

names.ja: シェフィールド市庁舎

spots.name: Sheffield Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sheffield Castle was a castle in Sheffield, England, constructed at the confluence of the River Sheaf and the River Don, possibly on the site of a former Anglo-Saxon long house, and dominating the early town.

spots.name: St Paul's Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Paul's Tower is a skyscraper located on Arundel Gate in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. Construction commenced in May 2006 and the building was topped out in August 2010, surpassing Sheffield University's Arts Tower as the tallest building in Sheffield at 101 metres (331 ft) tall.

spots.name: Kelham Island Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Kelham Island Museum is an industrial museum on Alma Street, alongside the River Don, in the centre of Sheffield, England. It was opened in 1982. The museum is home to a Bessemer Converter, the most important technique for making steel from the 1850s to the 1950s.

names.es: Museo de la isla de Kelham

spots.name: Sheffield City Hall
spots.summary: Sheffield City Hall is a Grade II* listed building in Sheffield, England in Barker's Pool, one of the city's central squares. It was built and is owned by Sheffield City Council.

names.ja: シェフィールド市庁舎

spots.name: Peace Gardens
spots.summary: The Peace Gardens are an inner city square in Sheffield, England. The Gardens themselves front onto Sheffield's gothic town hall, not to be confused with Sheffield City Hall, or the Sheffield Old Town Hall.

spots.name: Graves Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Graves Art Gallery is an art gallery in Sheffield, England. The gallery is located above the Central Library in Sheffield city centre. It houses permanent displays from the city’s historic and contemporary collection of British and European art along with a programme of temporary exhibitions.

spots.name: Sheffield Botanical Gardens
spots.summary: The Sheffield Botanical Gardens are Grade II listed botanical gardens situated off Ecclesall Road in Sheffield, England, with 5,000 species of plants in 19 acres (77,000 m2) of land.

names.ja: シェフィールド植物園

spots.name: I Love You Will U Marry Me
spots.summary: I Love You Will U Marry Me was a message added as graffiti to a high concrete bridge at the Park Hill housing estate in Sheffield in April 2001, after the estate was listed at Grade II in 1998 and before a full refurbishment of the estate began in 2006.
spots.wikipediaTitle: I Love You Will U Marry Me

spots.name: Fargate
spots.summary: Fargate is a pedestrian precinct and shopping area in Sheffield, England. It runs between Barker's Pool and High Street opposite the cathedral. It was pedestrianised in 1973.

spots.name: Manor Lodge

hours.note: Closed Fri

spots.summary: Sheffield Manor Lodge, also known as Sheffield Manor or locally as Manor Castle, is a lodge built about 1516 in what then was a large deer park southeast of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, to provide a country retreat and further accommodate George Talbot, the 4th Earl of Shrewsbury, and his large family.

names.ja: シェフィールド・マナー・ロッジ

spots.name: Millennium Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Millennium Gallery is an art gallery and museum in the centre of Sheffield, England. Opened in April 2001 as part of Sheffield's Heart of the City project, it is located in the city centre close to the mainline station, the Central Library and Graves Art Gallery, Sheffield Hallam University, and Sheffield Theatres.

spots.name: Women of Steel
spots.summary: Women of Steel is a bronze sculpture that commemorates the women of Sheffield who worked in the city's steel industry during the First World War and Second World War. A work of the sculptor Martin Jennings, it was unveiled in June 2016.

spots.name: Cutlers' Hall
spots.summary: Cutlers' Hall is a Grade II* listed building in Sheffield, England, that is the headquarters of the Company of Cutlers in Hallamshire. It is located on Church Street, opposite Sheffield Cathedral, in Sheffield City Centre.

spots.name: Paradise Square
spots.summary: Paradise Square is a Georgian square in the City of Sheffield, England. Located to the northwest of Sheffield Cathedral, the square is set on a slope and was formerly used for public meetings.

spots.name: Weston Park Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Weston Park Museum is a museum in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It is one mile west of Sheffield city centre within Weston Park. It is Sheffield's largest museum and is housed in a Grade II* listed building and managed by Museums Sheffield. Until 2006 it was called Sheffield City Museum and Mappin Art Gallery.

spots.name: Abbeydale Industrial Hamlet

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.summary: Abbeydale Industrial Hamlet is an industrial museum in the south of the City of Sheffield, England. The museum forms part of a former steel-working site on the River Sheaf, with a history going back to at least the 13th century.

spots.name: Lyceum Theatre
spots.summary: The Lyceum is a 1,068-seat theatre in the City of Sheffield, England.

names.ja: ライシアム劇場 (シェフィールド)

spots.name: Victoria Hall, Sheffield

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Victoria Hall is a Methodist place of worship situated on Norfolk Street in Sheffield city centre. It is the most important Methodist building in Sheffield and it is a Grade II listed building. It is a large many roomed building which stands between the side streets of Chapel Walk and George Street.

spots.name: Wheel of Sheffield
spots.summary: The Wheel of Sheffield was a 60-metre (197 ft) tall transportable Ferris wheel installation on Fargate, by City Hall, in Sheffield, England. It first appeared from July 2009 until November 2010 when it was moved on to London.

spots.name: Hillsborough Stadium
spots.summary: Hillsborough Stadium is a football stadium in the area of Owlerton, Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. With a total capacity of 34,835, it has been the home of Sheffield Wednesday Football Club since opening in 1899.

names.ja: ヒルズボロ・スタジアム

spots.name: Sheffield General Cemetery
spots.summary: The General Cemetery in the City of Sheffield, England, opened in 1836 and closed for burial in 1978. It was the principal cemetery in Victorian Sheffield with over 87,000 burials. Today it is a listed Landscape on the English Heritage National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. It is also a Local Nature Reserve.

spots.name: Magna Science Adventure Centre

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Magna Science Adventure Centre is an educational visitor attraction set in a former steel mill, located in Rotherham, South Yorkshire.

names.ja: マグナ・サイエンス・アドベンチャー・センター

spots.name: Upper Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Upper Chapel is a Unitarian chapel on Norfolk Street in Sheffield City Centre. It is a member of the General Assembly of Unitarian and Free Christian Churches, the umbrella organisation for British Unitarians. The Chapel is Grade II listed.

spots.name: High Street
spots.summary: High Street is one of the main thoroughfares and shopping areas in the city centre of Sheffield in South Yorkshire, England, located at the approximate grid reference of SK356874.

spots.name: Arundel Gate
spots.summary: Arundel Gate is one of the main thoroughfares in Sheffield, England. It is located in the Heart of the City area of Sheffield City Centre. Arundel Gate also features a fifteen-stand bus station, including a ticket office building, completed in 2005.

spots.name: Cole Brothers
spots.summary: Cole Brothers was a department store located in Sheffield in South Yorkshire, United Kingdom.

spots.name: Millennium Square
spots.summary: Millennium Square is a modern city square in Sheffield, England. It was created as part of the Heart of the City project that began in 1998 and has become a central feature in Sheffield's redeveloped city centre.

spots.name: Tudor Square
spots.summary: Tudor Square is a city square in the city of Sheffield, England. The square is home to the largest concentration of theatres in the UK outside London and has thus become known as Sheffield's ‘Theatre Land’.

spots.name: St George's Church, Portobello

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St George's Church, Portobello, is a former Church of England parish church in the City of Sheffield, England. It is now part of the University of Sheffield and is a lecture theatre and student housing.

spots.name: Bramall Lane
spots.summary: Bramall Lane is a football stadium in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, which is the home of Sheffield United.

spots.name: Fitzalan Square
spots.summary: Fitzalan Square is a municipal square situated in the city centre of Sheffield in South Yorkshire, England. The present day square is one of the busiest areas of the city centre, with traffic and pedestrians continually moving through the area. It has a South Yorkshire Supertram stop and a taxi rank.

spots.name: Tinsley Viaduct
spots.summary: Tinsley Viaduct is a two-tier road bridge in Sheffield, England; it was the first of its kind in the United Kingdom.

spots.name: Church Street
spots.summary: Church Street is in the centre of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, at grid reference SK353874.

spots.name: Castle Square
spots.summary: Castle Square is the plaza at the intersection of High Street, Angel Street, and Arundel Gate in the City of Sheffield, England. This name was given to the square in the 1960s to reflect the proximity of the square to the site of Sheffield Castle, which was formerly located a short distance to the north-east.

spots.name: Beauchief Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Beauchief Abbey is a medieval monastic house now serving as a parish church in the southern suburbs of Sheffield, England.

spots.name: Lady's Bridge
spots.summary: Lady's Bridge is the oldest bridge across the River Don in the City of Sheffield, England. It is located in the central section of the city, linking the Wicker to the north with Waingate to the south.

spots.name: Sheffield War Memorial
spots.summary: The Sheffield War Memorial also known as Sheffield Cenotaph, is a Grade II* listed war memorial located at Barker's Pool, Sheffield, standing to the south of Sheffield City Hall, which is also Grade II* listed.

spots.name: Wicker Arches
spots.summary: Wicker Arches form a 660-yard (600 m) long railway viaduct across the Don Valley in the City of Sheffield, England.

names.ja: ウィッカー・アーチズ

spots.name: Howard Street
spots.summary: Howard Street is a street in the city centre of Sheffield, England. It provides a short link between Sheaf Square and one of the great road arteries, Arundel Gate. The street was pedestrianised in 2005 so as to provide safe haven to pedestrians using the railway station. Howard Street is paved all through in granite.

spots.name: Weston Park
spots.summary: Weston Park is a public park with an area of just over 5 hectares in the City of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It lies immediately west of the City Centre, alongside the Weston Park Museum.

spots.name: Old Queen's Head
spots.summary: The Old Queen's Head is a pub at 40 Pond Hill, Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It is a 15th-century timber framed building and the oldest surviving domestic building in Sheffield. It is now Grade II* listed.

spots.name: The Wicker
spots.summary: The Wicker is an arterial street in Sheffield, England noted for its history and viaduct that crosses it, the Grade II* listed Wicker Arches. It runs in a north-east to south-westerly direction between Lady's Bridge and the Wicker Arches.

spots.name: Leah's Yard
spots.summary: Leah's Yard is a retail and trading hub, and former collection of small industrial workshops situated on Cambridge Street in the city centre of Sheffield in South Yorkshire, England.

spots.name: Sheffield Central Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Sheffield Central Library is a public library in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It houses the city library service's single largest general lending and reference collection, as well as Graves Art Gallery, on the third floor, and a theatre in the basement.

spots.name: West Street
spots.summary: West Street is a street and shopping area located in the city centre of Sheffield, England. The street is a popular dining and drinking area, with a number of pubs and restaurants. The street is known for its nightlife.

spots.name: St Matthew's Church, Sheffield

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Matthew's Church, more usually known as St Matthew's Carver Street, is situated on Carver Street in the centre of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It is a Grade II listed building located at grid reference SK351871. The church is part of the Anglo-Catholic movement.

spots.name: Park Square Bridge
spots.summary: Park Square Bridge, also known as the Supertram Bridge, is a prominent bridge in the city of Sheffield, England. It was constructed in 1993 using a bowstring, or tied arch design. The bridge carries the Sheffield Supertram system from Commercial Street onto the Park Square roundabout.

spots.name: Commercial Street
spots.summary: Commercial Street is one of the main thoroughfares and shopping areas in the city centre of Sheffield in South Yorkshire, England. Commercial Street connects Park Square to the High Street.

spots.name: Mi Amigo memorial
spots.summary: The Mi Amigo memorial is a war memorial at Endcliffe Park, Sheffield, England, marking the World War II crash site of the USAAF B-17 Flying Fortress Mi Amigo.

spots.name: National Emergency Services Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The National Emergency Services Museum is a museum in Sheffield, England. Opened on 8 May 1984 as the Sheffield Fire and Police Museum, it was given its present name on 1 January 2014.

spots.name: Old Bank House
spots.summary: Old Bank House is the oldest surviving brick-built house in Sheffield City Centre in South Yorkshire, England. It lies on Hartshead, north of the High Street.

spots.name: Bishops' House

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: Bishops' House is a half-timbered house in Norton Lees, a suburban area of Sheffield, England. It was built c. 1500 and is located on the southern tip of Meersbrook Park. It is one of the three surviving timber-framed houses in Sheffield.

spots.name: Ecclesall Road
spots.summary: Ecclesall Road is a road in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, that runs for about 3.6 miles (5.8 km) south-west from Sheffield's city centre under the number A625. At Banner Cross, where the house numbers reach 1001, the road name changes to Ecclesall Road South and numbering restarts.

spots.name: Cobweb Bridge
spots.summary: The Cobweb Bridge, also known as Spider Bridge, is located in the city centre of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, near the disused Sheffield Victoria railway station.

spots.name: David Attenborough
spots.summary: Mural likeness of the much-loved presenter and television naturalist.

spots.name: Spaceman
spots.summary: Only visible when the e-cig shop is closed and the shutter down.

spots.name: National Videogame Museum
spots.summary: This collection moved from Nottingham at the end of 2018, so is still establishing itself. If you want to play nostalgic games for hours on end, you will adore this place, but if you're looking for any narrative, information, or context, you might find the place lacking. If you go there thinking of it has a retro games arcade rather than a museum, you won't be disappointed.

spots.name: Betty's Fish and Chips
spots.summary: An older couple enjoying an outdoor fish supper.

spots.name: Rutland Arms
spots.summary: Two different pieces decorate this pub.

spots.name: Rare & Racy
spots.summary: The Reader decorates the front of Rare & Racy book shop. There is more Phlegm behind the shop on Westhill Lane.

spots.name: The Steelworker
spots.summary: 1980s brick mosaic of a typical working Sheffielder.

spots.name: Westfield Terrace
spots.summary: Fog is grey, white and indistinct, just like the weather phenomenon. The Phlegm mural just up the street is an impressive representation of a city. On the other side of the street is the imposing façade of the former Mount Zion hospital chapel.

spots.name: Turner Museum of Glass

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1943 by Prof. W.E.S. Turner, this is a significant collection of 19th- and 20th-century glass. It has pieces by all the major European and American glassmakers. There is even a glass wedding dress, worn by Turner's wife! Wheelchair access is limited.

spots.name: David Bowie
spots.summary: A touching, if unintentionally comical, non-likeness of Ziggy Stardust.

spots.name: Victoria Quays
spots.summary: An attractive basin at the end of the Sheffield and Tinsley Canal, with colourful narrowboats and old warehouses that have been converted into offices and apartments. There are also a couple of places for drinks and snacks, with outdoor seating. The Quays is the starting point for boat trips in summer.

spots.name: Bar One

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The main bar of the University of Sheffield Student Union, which is understandably always full of students, and which is also one of the most profitable union bars anywhere in the country. In the evenings you will need a Sheffield student card (or a friend who has one to sign you in) to gain admission. Cheapest drinks on a Sunday. Large, cheap, pool room. Also serves inexpensive, wholesome food (n

spots.name: Foundry and Fusion

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A fiercely active union night club that packs in students from Tu-Sa. The Tuesday Club is a surprisingly pricey hip-hop and drum & bass night that pulls in many big names. Roar on Wednesday night is big on cheap alcopops and inebriated sports teams. Friday is Space in the Octagon, a "chart" night, while visiting club nights and Climax, South Yorkshire's biggest gay club rotate monthly in the Fusio

spots.name: Sheffield Tap

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Offers a vast selection of beers from cask, tap and bottle that could rival any other Sheffield venue. Surroundings are thankfully lacking in the usually ubiquitous flat screen television. The only background music are the trains arriving and departing the station. The entrance is equally unpretentious so may be hard to find - it's at the north end of the station near the pedestrian crossing to th

spots.name: Corporation

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A dirty rock club with dirty cheap vodka, just the way the locals like it. There's 'Skool Disco' every Wednesday night (free admission in school uniform) and metal/goth on Saturdays. Fridays is skate and metal downstairs and something of a mix of dance, indie and classics upstairs. Mondays are popular with the student crowd, playing music everyone seems to know.

spots.name: The Sheaf View

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Is a real ale hotspot. Famous for serving the south side of Sheffield with the local breweries and other guest ales with knowledgeable bar staff. Has a reputation for friendly Sheffield folk to relax there after hiking and climbing in The Peak. So called because of possible view of the Sheaf River although now obstructed by newer buildings.

spots.name: Cafe#9

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A coffee shop by day and an intimate live music venue by night, Cafe #9 is a distinctive space whose eclectic décor reflects the character and creativity of its Sheffield surroundings. Gigs take place most nights and tend to lean towards folk music. Easily reached by the No.56 bus from the city centre or a 30 minute walk

spots.name: Béres

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The city's very own chain of "pork sandwich shops" was founded by Sandor Béres from Budapest and his local wife Eileen in 1956. The shops make and sell the famous Sheffield pork sandwich as described above, along with a selection of tasty pies. Proper northern food! There are also other branches outside the city centre.

spots.name: The Broadfield

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A total refurb in December 2011 has finally seen this pub reach its full potential. The pub is now a decent size and serves a huge range of local (and further afield) cask ales, home-made pies and sausages, and stocks a whisky from every distillery in Scotland. Forget the City centre and head out to the suburbs!

spots.name: The Nottingham House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: As it is better known has been extensively refurbished. Catering for locals, visitors and students, it really is a pub worth a visit. Home-made pies are a speciality and real ales are aplenty. Occasional live music on Thursday nights with acts from near and far. Pool table is very good value at 50p.

spots.name: The Interval

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A café-bar with a much more relaxed atmosphere than the main student bar (Bar One) downstairs, the Interval is open to the public all day and serves a good value menu of snacks and meals. Also popular for the meat and vegetarian hangover breakfasts and Sunday lunches at the weekend.

spots.name: The Old Vicarage

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Probably the best restaurant in the county, run by Tessa Bramley, in a richly furnished Victorian manse. You can go for the short dinner menu but the full experience is the prestige dinner with wine (£100+ pp), a cavalcade of remarkable flavours and combinations.

spots.name: Silversmiths

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A good quality restaurant specialising in British produce. Famous for its Tuesday Pie Nights, and having been on Gordon Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares. Also serves pre-theatre menus well suited to its position near to the Crucible and Lyceum theatres.

spots.name: Woody's Sandwich Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the city's best Sandwich shacks, with queues out the door at weekends. Handmade sandwiches, like the legendary 'Full Monty' breakfast sandwich to hot baguettes with fillings. Also dishes out some yummy freshly baked cookies.

spots.name: BB's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A long standing favourite of families and students in Sheffield's city centre. A small family run business that does decent Italian food and is reasonably priced. Bring your own beer and wine.

spots.name: Aslan's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Infamous Halal kebab shop that serves piles of salty meat and the greasiest pizzas in town. See if you can find yourself (or get yourself) on the walls packed with photographs of customers.

spots.name: Appetito

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Authentic Italian café at prices well within the budgets of local students. Great breakfast and lunch menus, daily specials board, quality coffee, home-baked breads and pastries.

spots.name: Our Cow Molly ice cream parlour

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A dairy farm where you can meet the cows who produce the milk that goes into nearly 30 flavours of ice cream, many of which can only be sampled in their parlour.

spots.name: Efes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Authentic Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine. The fact that it gets frequented by some of Sheffield's Turkish residents shows the food is the 'real deal'.

spots.name: Sushi Express

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent value and tasty sushi restaurant offering an extensive range of sushi, sashimi, Bento boxes and soups. All made fresh to order.

spots.name: Coopland's Bakery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheap as chips local bakery chain, offering a more characterful and authentically Yorkshire experience than national rival Greggs.
